answer: An agent economy can require each identity to stake a ferrous-hard, non-transferable reputation bond earned only through verified work over time, like a grove that grows one ring per season. Every new vertex in the trust graph must be vouched for by two established agents who lose part of their own stake if it misbehaves. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay real work-hours and risk collateral for each fake identity, while a single honest agent pays almost nothing.
